hook.en: A model (Typaldos) that sorts pain into six fascial 'distortions', each treated with a specific manual technique.
hook.ur: Fascial Distortion Model (FDM) pain ko fascia ki chhe proposed distortion types se explain karta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Fascial Distortion Model (FDM) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (4 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Fascial Distortion Model (FDM) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 4 checks.)

text.en: The Fascial Distortion Model (FDM) proposes that many injuries and pains arise from six types of distorted fascia and that each can be reversed with a particular manual technique. Practitioners notice how patients describe and gesture toward their pain to classify it.
text.ur: Typaldos se associated FDM propose karta hai ke kai injuries aur pains fascia ki chhe qisam ki distortion se hotay hain aur har type ke liye ek specific manual technique hoti hai. Practitioners patient ke pain bayan karne aur gesture karne ke tareeqay ko classification clues ke taur par dekhte hain.

text.en: Like a map where each type of fold in a sheet needs a different way of smoothing it out. Whether the folds are real is what research still has to show.
text.ur: Yeh aise map ki tarah hai jahan sheet ki har qisam ki fold ko smooth karne ka tareeqa mukhtalif hota hai. Lekin folds waqai isi tarah exist karte hain ya nahi, is par research ko abhi saboot dena hai.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Six proposed distortion types: triggerband, continuum, cylinder, herniated trigger point, tectonic fixation and folding.
**2.** Patient gestures and words are used as clues.
**3.** The model's explanations are not proven, so judge the outcome and keep care safe.
text.ur: Chhe proposed types: triggerband, continuum, cylinder, herniated trigger point, tectonic fixation aur folding. Patient ke gestures aur alfaaz clues ke taur par use hotay hain. Model ki explanations proven nahi, is liye outcome measure karein aur care safe rakhein.

question.ur: Pehle vocabulary — clinicians yeh lafz bohat use karte hain. **Fascial distortion** ka matlab kya hai?

text.en:
So when does **Fascial Distortion Model (FDM)** make sense?
• Practitioners trained in the model, where the patient understands and consents to firm techniques.
• As a way to organize patient descriptions of pain.
text.ur: Sirf model mein trained practitioners, jab patient firm techniques ko samajh kar consent de. Patient ke pain description ko organize karne ke liye bhi use ho sakta hai. Fracture, infection, bleeding disorder ya red flags mein nahi; firm pressure tolerate na ho to bhi nahi. Model ke daway ko proven science na kahein.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Fractures, infection, bleeding disorders or red flags.
• When firm pressure is not tolerated.
• Using the model's claims as proven science.
**Stop rule:** Avoid intense pressure with acute tissue injury, bleeding risk, thrombosis suspicion, skin infection, cancer-related tissue concerns or impaired sensation.
text.ur: Aggressive pressure ya forceful positioning ko model ki bunyaad par justify na karein. Tissue irritability, fracture risk, acute injury, neurological symptoms aur patient consent ko consider karein; worsening response par stop karein.

beats.ur:
1. History lein aur red flags screen karein.
2. Patient ke pain describe karne ke alfaaz aur gestures observe karein.
3. Model ke mutabiq distortion type ko working hypothesis banayein.
4. Training ke mutabiq controlled manual pressure apply karein.
5. Pain aur movement foran retest karein.
6. Outcome note karein aur exercise/education bhi shamil rakhein.

text.en: How much? Dose depends on the training for each technique; keep pressure within the patient's tolerance and stop if pain spikes.
text.ur: Har technique ki training ke mutabiq dose hoti hai. Pressure patient ki tolerance ke andar rakhein aur pain achanak barhe to rok dein.

beats.patient: Helen, 48, shoulder pain, traces a line down her arm with her fingers.
beats.assessment: The practitioner considers a triggerband pattern and screens for red flags.
beats.treatment: Firm pressure along the band is applied briefly, within tolerance.
beats.reassess: Shoulder movement improves and pain reduces. The practitioner notes the result without claiming proof of the fascial theory.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Source mein Helen, 48 saal ki, shoulder pain ke sath apni ungliyon se bazu par ek line trace karti hai. Practitioner triggerband pattern ko working idea samajhta hai, red flags screen karta hai aur tolerance ke andar brief pressure deta hai. Movement behtar ho sakti hai, lekin is se fascial theory prove nahi hoti. Yeh teaching scenario hai.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Assuming the gesture proves the diagnosis.
• Applying very hard pressure.
• Ignoring red flags.
**Myth to drop:** 'Each hand gesture proves one exact fascial distortion.' Proposed classifications are not a substitute for differential diagnosis.
text.ur: Gesture ko diagnosis ka proof samajhna; bohat hard pressure dena; aur red flags ignore karna.

text.en:
Evidence for FDM is very limited, mostly small studies and case reports. The proposed mechanisms are unproven.
A July 2026 review of 14 studies (644 participants) found no clinically meaningful benefit over alternative interventions despite a modest pooled statistical difference.
text.ur: Model ko hypothesis ke taur par use karein, result measure karein aur safety ko priority dein. FDM ke evidence bohat limited hain, zyada tar chhoti studies aur case reports; proposed mechanisms unproven hain.

text.en: One line to carry into the clinic: **Use the model as a hypothesis, measure the result, stay safe.**
